chapter: Gene Mayl, Teddy Buckner and the Dixie Flies
title: Success at the Lark and Swede Jensen's album
summary: The band had a twelve-week contract; Swede Jensen, a machine shop owner, offered to record an album for his own use.

bands.name: Joe Darensbourg and His Dixie Flies

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Did you have much success with your band, the Dixie Flies?

It had pretty good success, yeah. In fact, I had a twelve-week contract to go into the Lark, which was good -- we had a lot of people. I was approached by a guy named Swede Jensen, that owned a machine shop, just

to make an album -- as a hobby. Just for his own use is what he said. And in the meantime, I had started playing "Yellow Dog Blues." Ory never would record it. When I was with Ory, I always wanted him to record it.
